correctness.rationale: Under any infinite field K and ordinary K-rational automorphisms, the two-dimensional characteristic-two algebra e1^2=e2^2=e1 has nonzero squares, only identity automorphism, and infinitely many pairwise inequivalent orthogonal bases f1(a),f2(a) with at most two parameters per scaling-permutation class. In any characteristic, the three-dimensional algebra e1^2=e2^2=e1+e3, e3^2=e2+e3 has only identity automorphism: applying T to products forces T(e1),T(e2) into span(e1,e2), then T(e3)=ce3, and preservation of e1^2 and e3^2 forces identity. In characteristic !=2, stereographic rational SO2 rotations give infinitely many distinct natural-basis classes over any infinite K. Dimension one has a single class. A nondegenerate two-dimensional nonperfect algebra in char !=2 has xy=B(x,y)u with nonsingular symmetric B, and either a nonidentity reflection fixing nonisotropic u or a nonidentity hyperbolic similarity scaling isotropic u; a perfect algebra only admits monomial natural basis changes. Thus d(K)=2 in char2 and 3 otherwise. Independently enumerated invertible matrices and automorphisms in F2 (3D, 168 GL members) and F3 (3D, 11232) as finite corroboration only; all-field proof is algebraic.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for the full d(K) formula with ordinary automorphism group exactly identity. Important predecessor: evolution algebras with infinitely many natural bases and finite nontrivial automorphism group already exist (2D over complex fields, group order 2), so the weaker Question 14 existence is not independently new. Existing survey Proposition 14 uses infinite orthogonal group, and nondegenerate classification does not state the sharp all-infinite-field trivial-group minimum. Resultary E_lambda jump is distinct.
residual_risks: A general classification of 2D/3D evolution algebras may implicitly contain the same minimality when combined with automorphism formulae.
Published answer to the *weaker* finite-not-trivial automorphism existence question overlaps the motivation; no independent priority for that weaker existence result is claimed.

value.rationale: The survey poses an explicit rigidity-versus-natural-basis question, and the characteristic-dependent *minimum dimension with trivial ordinary automorphism group* across all infinite fields is a sharp, natural invariant. It distinguishes a finite nontrivial group from complete rigidity and handles the subtle characteristic-two exceptional dimension; there is substantive structural content beyond an example.

limitations: Infinite fields only; finite fields cannot have infinitely many natural bases.
Triviality concerns ordinary K-point automorphism groups, not automorphism group schemes or base extensions.
Prior work apparently resolves weaker mere finite-group existence over some fields; novelty is the sharper universal trivial-group minimum.
residual_risks: A general classification of 2D/3D evolution algebras may implicitly contain the same minimality when combined with automorphism formulae.
Published answer to the *weaker* finite-not-trivial automorphism existence question overlaps the motivation; no independent priority for that weaker existence result is claimed.
